what: Clear blue sky as a test surface for Digital Aerochrome: sky radiance relative to the midday sunlight the fit uses (filter-data.json 'ill', AM1.5 global), 10nm steps 300-1100nm, scaled so 550nm matches the previous estimate's brightness (0.2241). Shape only matters; the fit normalises exposure.
source: Kider, Knowlton, Newlin, Li and Greenberg, 'A Framework for the Experimental Comparison of Solar and Skydome Illumination', ACM Transactions on Graphics 33(6), SIGGRAPH Asia 2014. Data: https://github.com/spectralskylight/sky-measurements-2014 (Apache License 2.0). Measured with an ASD spectroradiometer, 350-2500nm at 1nm, 81 sky directions per capture, roof of Rhodes Hall, Cornell University.
method: Per capture: directions at least 20 degrees above the horizon, the brightest 30% at 550nm dropped (the sky around the sun), each remaining spectrum averaged into 10nm steps and divided by its own 550nm value, median over directions; median over the four captures; divided by the AM1.5 global sunlight; the O2 and water-vapour bands (715-735, 750-775, 925-965nm), where the two instruments resolve the absorption differently, bridged by interpolation in log space; a 3-point median then 3-point mean smooth; below 350nm (the instrument's first channel) the 350nm value is held. The four captures agree within 3% from 500 to 600nm, about 10% at 400 and 850nm, and 13-18% past 900nm.
